cases.title: “Ask about this” on the Mobile tile
cases.question: What has Brad built on mobile?
cases.answer: Brad has built a range of mobile work across several roles. At Hopper, Brad co-architected and built RemoteUI, a server-driven UI framework rendered natively with Jetpack Compose and MVVM on Android and SwiftUI on iOS. At Bottle Rocket, Brad shipped native Android apps in Java and Kotlin for brands including Coca-Cola Freestyle, AskPETMD, Starwood SPG and Chewy. At BookShout, Brad rebuilt the ebook reader on a recycled-WebView architecture for more efficient navigation and rendering. Brad also built VINDecoded, where it is one product on three platforms. A React web app runs in the browser and inside both mobile apps. Native Android (Kotlin) and iOS (SwiftUI) shells add what the web can't do.

cases.title: “Ask about this” on the Full-stack tile
cases.question: What has Brad built across the stack?
cases.answer: Brad has built across mobile, web, backend and AI work. On the Android side, Brad shipped native Android apps in Java and Kotlin for brands including Coca-Cola Freestyle, AskPETMD, Starwood SPG and Chewy. At Hopper, Brad co-architected and built RemoteUI, a server-driven UI framework rendered natively with Jetpack Compose and MVVM on Android and SwiftUI on iOS, and delivered Disruption Assistance end to end: the RFC and ADR, stakeholder alignment, new services on Terraform-provisioned GCP, backend APIs, a payment flow with rewards points, offer generation and Redis caching, and the React front end. For VINDecoded, Brad re-platformed the app from AngularJS/Cordova to a React/TypeScript web app, native Android and iOS apps, and a Node.js/TypeScript API backed by SQL, Firebase, Azure and cloud analytics.

cases.title: “Ask about this” on the Applied AI tile
cases.question: What AI work has Brad shipped?
cases.answer: Brad has shipped several AI features. At VINDecoded, Shipped production AI features: grounded streaming vehicle chat, with provider-switchable models and tool-isolated vehicle data; vision-based VIN, plate and gas-receipt scanning with structured outputs. At Hopper, Worked directly with the CEO, revenue leaders and the Fintech VP to launch a flight-shopping assistant and generative offers that matched or exceeded static-offer attach rates. Brad also built a human-approved experimentation loop on LaunchDarkly, Amplitude and BigQuery telemetry. It generates UI, code, pull requests and visual/browser tests, releases behind flags, and monitors outcomes for promotion or rollback.

cases.title: “Ask about this” on “Vehicle-history and research platform”
cases.question: Tell me more about this: “A profitable vehicle-history and research platform for shoppers, owners and sellers.”
cases.answer: The visitor is asking about the VINDecoded description. The document gives this context: A profitable vehicle-history and research platform for shoppers, owners and sellers. The product itself is described as follows: VINDecoded turns a VIN or a license plate into what a person needs to know about a car: specs, recalls, market value, the window sticker and its history report. Owners also use it to track maintenance, fuel and recalls, and to read their car through an OBD-II adapter. It runs as one product on three platforms. A React web app runs in the browser and inside both mobile apps. Native Android (Kotlin) and iOS (SwiftUI) shells add what the web can't do: Bluetooth to the car, store billing, ads and the camera. It earns money from ads, one-time reports, credits and memberships.

cases.title: “Ask about this” on “Design, code and process, all public”
cases.question: Tell me more about this: “A résumé you can explore, built in the open: its design, code and process are all public.”
cases.answer: The site describes itself this way: A résumé you can explore, built in the open: its design, code and process are all public. The documents add some detail on the process. Each feature starts as a spec Brad approves. Tests come from its scenarios before the code, a reviewer in a fresh context checks the change, and nothing reaches main until Brad says push. On releases, each release goes out from a tag Brad approves, with a rollback ready and a written record. The site is built with Astro, React, Tailwind CSS and TypeScript, and served by Firebase Hosting.
